title: The Two Singhs Rush Into Unequal Combat

blocks.text: Negotiation is dismissed with contempt, because the Singhs say they have no business in court when the issue is already settled by tyranny and resistance. Instead they rush the Mughal force with staffs, stones, and spears, turning improvised weapons into marks of fearless resolve.

The page delights in the disproportion of the contest. Against cavalry and trained troops, the Singhs move with the suddenness of a lion and refuse to give the enemy the psychological victory of seeing them hesitate.

Every fresh attack only hardens their stance. The underlying point is that martyr courage had already stripped death of its terror, so numerical inferiority no longer controls the shape of the battle.
